#4274. Xbox Announces Two New Methods To Play Games Through The Cloud

"Starting today, we’re rolling out two previews for XBOX Cloud Gaming."

Team Xbox continues to make improvements to playing games through the cloud, and they've just announced two new methods for doing just that - both launching in "preview" form later today.

The first of these is the ability to use your phone as a controller, which will be available across Android and iOS on supported Smart TVs (including certain Amazon, LG, Samsung and other models) in this preview.

To access this, you'll just need to turn on the "Preview Features" in the Xbox app on your supported TV:

To try it, turn on Preview Features under Settings > Account in the latest supported Smart TV experience. When you launch a game without a physical controller connected, you’ll see an option to use your phone for that session.

The second new method is something called "cloud connect", which allows you to connect using Wi-Fi to reduce input latency in Xbox Cloud Gaming titles. The catch here is that it only works with the new Xbox Nano Controller for now, and even then it "won’t work with every cloud gaming experience yet" during the preview phase.

Here's a bit more about it, along with an image:

Players in the U.S. can preview cloud connect with the XBOX Nano Controller starting today. Instead of a Bluetooth connection to your TV, cloud connect uses your Wi-Fi to connect directly to the cloud server running your game. That can help reduce input latency, so gameplay may feel more responsive. Cloud connect is still an early test, so it won’t work with every cloud gaming experience yet. For now, you can try it on supported Smart TVs and the web.

For what it's worth, it's been rumoured by Windows Central that the "cloud connect" feature will become part of all Xbox controllers in the future, but for the time being it remains exclusive to the Nano.

So, there you go! It seems these will remain in a preview state for a decent amount of time as the team aims to "shape the experience", so be sure to provide feedback if you have any improvements in mind.

We'll leave you with a related story about the new Nano controller that released today down below.

#4273. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4271. PS6 Development on Track, Sony Making 'Solid Progress' Towards Next-Gen

Work on the PS6 and the next console generation as a whole is currently "progressing as scheduled" at PlayStation, it's been confirmed.

Speaking alongside the release of Sony's latest quarterly financial results, CFO Lin Tao said the company is on track to deliver its next PlayStation system, and it intends to make "solid progress" towards the next generation within the next fiscal year (via VGC).

The quote from Tao reads: "Looking ahead to the next fiscal year, we aim to continue to enhance user engagement and further strengthen monetisation through the release of strong titles and the expansion of our service. We also intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

Tao continued by talking up "investment in the new platform" from the start of the next fiscal year. It has to attach "great importance" to a new console and "make the necessary investments" for it. "We have to support the soundness of our platform and think about how rationally we can invest in that platform. We will announce that at an appropriate time in the future."

A few months ago, Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki claimed the firm hadn't yet decided when the PS6 will come out. Consistent rumours point to a release in the next few years, however, with a potential $1,000+ price point and a handheld device to go with it.

With the prices of components still on the rise — which Sony would need to manufacture PS6 hardware — the potential cost of a next-gen machine looks like it'll be the biggest factor in whether PlayStation fans jump on board or not. When we polled Push Square users, 65% of you said you wouldn't pay four figures for a video game console.

Microsoft will also have a new Xbox to launch in the coming years, currently codenamed Xbox Helix, and that's suggested to cost as much as $1,800, depending on whether it decides to subsidise the box. PS6 is at least rumoured to be cheaper to make than Xbox Helix, so the cost shouldn't get quite that high.

Elsewhere in its financial report, Sony confirmed PS5 sales have reached 97.9 million. With a boost from GTA 6, it should hit the 100 million sales milestone by the end of the next quarter, and become the fourth PlayStation system to do so.

@sanderson72 that financial bull was always being released, but the media wasn’t reporting it.

It’s not aimed at customers but investors and such calls have always occurred.

Due to insatiable demand from gamers for any scrap of info, and the games media looking for clicks, these investor calls are now published and picked apart by the media for any juicy snippets. Often the media blow innocuous statements out of proportion and read imaginary conclusions between the lines to create a good story.

In the old days you’d read about this stuff in Edge Magazine, but not your tabloid gaming mags. That persisted into the internet era but over the last Gen or two it’s started to be more prominently reported on the mass consumption consumer websites as opposed to just industry sites.

#4270. We Have So Many Questions About This Stellar Blade Launch Trailer

Shift Up has launched a new live-action launch trailer for Stellar Blade: Complete Edition on Switch 2, and it's... well, we have so many questions.

To be fair, the message is clear: take EVE wherever you go, right? It's a nod toward the Switch 2's portable nature, though why EVE is interrupting someone's gaming session to brush their teeth is a bit odd now, isn't it?

We're also a bit puzzled as to why the ad goes for the 4:3 aspect ratio. It's not particularly cinematic or anything, so it doesn't make a whole lot of sense.

Despite our questions, however, it's a fun little ad. Harmless, y'know, and certainly a lot better than the AI-generated slop Shift Up posted to advertise its upcoming sequel.

Stellar Blade: Complete Edition is out now for the Switch 2. We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review, praising the combat and exploration, though noting that the visuals and performance aren't quite as good as we'd hoped.

#4268. Full FC 26 Team of the Year promo brings free Hero upgrades and another unstoppable Claudia Pina

The FC 26 Team of the Year brings new end-game special cards for meta favourites and Icons, as well as upgrades for free Heroes.

EA Sports has revealed the much-anticipated Ultimate Team of the Year cards for the 2025/26 season, including a slew of meta favourites from the likes of the evergreen Virgil van Dijk, super-fast Kylian Mbappe and unplayable queen of FC 26 Claudia Pina.

Elsewhere Lionesses Alessia Russo, Lucy Bronze and Leah Williamson feature alongside now-obligatory Barcelona duo Alexia Putellas and Aitana Bonmati. On the men’s side, Arsenal’s title tilt sees Declan Rice and William Saliba make the first 11, while Champions League holders PSG have the most players from a single team, with Ousmane Dembele, Vitinha and Nuno Mendes adding both rapid speed and technical prowess to proceedings.

However, the Team of the Year selection hasn’t been without controversy. The FC 26 TOTY promo is voted for by players, you probably cast your vote by selecting time-limited gold cards yourself, but that method has led some to question whether the Team of the Year is more of a popularity contest than a true measure of performance. This is with specific reference to Virgil, whose in-and-out form during Liverpool’s poor start this season has caused some to question his eight-straight inclusion.

In yet another blow to those of us who got Mario Gomez and Gianluca Vialli from the Classic XI Hero pack, during the TOTY event these Classic XI Heroes will be further upgraded to TOTY Honorable Mentions Heroes.

More TOTY items will also be dropping over the next couple of weeks, including a men’s and women’s 12th player, Honorable Mentions, 2 teams of TOTY Icons and both a men’s and women’s “Captain of the Year”.

For more on how to get the best out of these players, check out our page on the best FC 26 formations and custom tactics.

#4267. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

The latest Nintendo Download update for North America has arrived, and it's bringing Ocarina of Time — but also other new games — to the eShop. As always, be sure to drop a vote in our poll and comment down below with your potential picks for the week. Enjoy!

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time - (Nintendo, 5th Nov, $59.99). The evil Ganondorf is scheming to steal the mythical Triforce from the Sacred Realm and take over the world. Now, Link must become the Hero of Time and save the kingdom of Hyrule. Enjoy completely overhauled visuals, orchestral music, voice acting and expanded cutscenes. Jump and dash through the action with enhanced controls and modern camera movements, making this a great entry point into this series! - Read our The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Stellar Blade Complete Edition (SHIFT UP, 5th Nov, $59.99) – Save humanity from extinction as EVE in this story-driven action adventure where you descend from the Colony to reclaim an Earth devastated by mysterious creatures known as the Naytiba. Featuring a blend of cinematic storytelling and gameplay, the game offers deep character progression with customizable skills, gear and combat builds for you to take into epic boss encounters. Players can enjoy the game at home or on the go, with immersive Joy-Con 2 motion controls for select non-combat activities like fishing. Additionally, this edition includes NieR:Automata and GODDESS OF VICTORY: NIKKE collaboration content, as well as costumes inspired by the Bayonetta series. - Read our Stellar Blade Complete Edition review

Review Stellar Blade: Complete Edition (Switch 2) - Perfectly Playable, Despite Drawbacks

Metaphor: ReFantazio (SEGA, 12th Nov, $39.99) – Enter the Tournament for the Throne and fight for the future in the next evolution of fantasy RPG. Control your destiny, face your fears and awaken magical “Archetype” powers that lie dormant in your heart. Team up with a compelling cast of characters and embark on an immersive journey that promises hours of exploration, unique combat systems featuring a blend of dynamic turn-based and real-time battles, and more.

RACCOIN: Chaos Max Edition (Playstack, 10th Nov, $11.99) – Push your luck and don’t get stuck in this coin-pusher roguelike. Combine special coin types with powerful items to trigger wild combos and send coins flying in pursuit of high scores. Play as eight distinct characters, each with their own themed coins and playstyles. The game supports Joy-Con 2 mouse controls, and there’s also an in-game arcade cabinet skin exclusive to the Nintendo Switch 2 version!

TANUKI: Pon’s Summer (Critical Reflex, 10th Nov, $19.99) - BMX your way into the hearts of the townsfolk as Pon, a well-meaning tanuki with a part-time job at the post office in this cozy life sim adventure. Deliver packages, compete in sports, make friends and carry out a variety of other activities as you restore the shrine for the Great Tanuki Festival before summer’s end.

Pokémon Pokopia Expansion Pass – Part 2: Dazzling Decorations – The next part of the Pokémon Pokopia - Expansion Pass paid DLC is slated to arrive Dec. 9, bringing some extra flair with in-game accessories to wear! Ditto isn’t the only one who can dress up, either: other Pokémon appearing in the game can sport these stylish accessories too!

Arcade Archives 2 SWIMMER (HAMSTER, 29th Oct, $9.99) - "SWIMMER" is an action game released by TEHKAN (KOEI TECMO GAMES) in 1982. Take control of the swimmer and see if you can make it to the treasure island. Use Power Pills and dive underwater to skillfully avoid obstacles and enemy monsters. The “Arcade Archives” series is developed with the concept of faithfully reproducing classic arcade games.

Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game (PM Studios, 29th Oct, $29.99) - Featuring hand-drawn 2D animation faithful to the series’ roots, Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game lets you experience the world of Avatar like never before. Choose from 12 playable characters and go head-to-head across a variety of modes, including Offline & Online Versus, Story, Arcade, Training, Spectator, and an Art Gallery.

Castlebound (Ogre Pixel, 11th Nov, $9.99) - Fight hordes of evil monsters and defend your castle in this 1-4 player action platformer with Roguelike elements! Castlebound is a thrilling roguelike action game where you and your allies must defend a walking castle while battling relentless waves of monstrous foes.

Chivalware (Dotemu, 5th Nov, $8.99) - Chivalware is a fast-paced action roguelite with tactical tile-matching mechanics. SLAY THE KING! You are a Disk Knight — a legendary warrior who wields weapon disks! The kingdom calls on you to slay its King, driven mad by power and years of isolation. But as you carve your way toward the castle, strange glitches suggest something deeper is at play… THE POWER OF FLOPPY DISKS!

Console Archives MARL JONG (HAMSTER, 29th Oct, $11.99) - *The game includes only the Japanese version. Please note that all in-game text is in Japanese only. "MARL JONG" was released by Nippon Ichi Software in 2003 for a 32-bit home console. This is a game in which you go on an adventure while competing in "MARL JONG" matches with the people of Marl Kingdom. With simple controls, gameplay progresses smoothly! Furthermore, you can enjoy heated battles using character-specific "Special Moves" and comeback-enabling “Cheat Techniques”. Demon Slayer -Kimetsu no Yaiba- The Hinokami Chronicles 2 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition (SEGA, 29th Oct, $39.99) - Single Player: Story Mode Play as Tanjiro and relive the Entertainment District Arc, the Swordsmith Village Arc, and the Hashira Training Arc from the TV anime, Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba! Battle Upper Rank demons with your allies! VS Mode: The Hashira Unite! The game features over 40 characters, including the nine Hashira, the highest-ranking swordsmen of the Demon Slayer Corps! Faraway (Annapurna Interactive, 5th Nov, $7.99) - Faraway is an endless procedurally generated, mastery-driven arcade game about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive. Connect stars to harvest their energy, extend your fleeting life, and build your score. Shape constellations freely, and take risks with advanced techniques to earn additional energy and points. Faraway’s simple rule-set and flowing controls are easy to approach but demanding to master. Every run begins from nothing, in a universe generated in real time around your performance.

Hasbro Games Junior Collection (Outright Games, 6th Nov, $29.99) - Play Monopoly Jr., Clue Jr., and The Game of Life Jr. Customize your avatar, unlock rewards, and enjoy local multiplayer fun for up to 4 players. Titanium Court (Fellow Traveller, 29th Oct, $11.24) - Well what do we have here? Streetwise tough looking for answers, huh. Well, answers we got, assuming you've got the second half of our agreement? Here's all the "dirt" we uncovered on this "Titanium Court": So, lotta people have heard of this game, but not a lot are coming clean about what it actually is. Most of the witnesses we "interviewed" just said it was "a fanciful rabbit-hole of unending delights" or some crap like that. Real coy operation they got going on over there, I'll tell ya what. Don't worry, we did manage to shake a few facts out of them. Here you go! Title: Titanium Court Developer: AP Thomson Publisher: Fellow Traveller Number of players: 1 Play time: 6-30 hours. ZERO PARADES: Director’s Cut (ZA/UM, 3rd Nov, $35.99) - From the creators of Disco Elysium comes ZERO PARADES - the acclaimed espionage RPG, now expanded with the DIRECTOR'S CUT. Review Zero Parades: Director's Cut (Switch 2) - ZA/UM Returns With Another Atmospheric, Cerebral Yet Overly Familiar RPG

A Snail’s Tale (Something Classic, 11th Nov, $12.99) - A retro RPG that asks the age old question: would you take a world of riches in exchange for being chased by an immortal, killer snail? Once upon a time, a commoner was granted his wish to become the king of a vast nation. In exchange, he is constantly chased by an immortal killer snail. Now the king is facing his end of the bargain.

Arcade Archives PREHISTORIC ISLE (HAMSTER, 29th Oct, $7.99) - "PREHISTORIC ISLE" is a shooting game released by SNK in 1989. As the protagonist heads to Greenhell Island to investigate a series of shipwrecks off the coast of the Bahamas, prehistoric dragons thought to have gone extinct launch a relentless attack. The option unit equipped to your aircraft can be repositioned to change its attack method into 5 different types based on its location, such as firing flame lasers upward or dropping bombs diagonally downward. Make full use of your option unit to face various obstacles and uncover the truth behind the mysterious shipwrecks!

Big Jhow Jet (Nerd Games, 7th Nov, $6.99) - Prepare for takeoff! Strap on your homemade jetpack, defy gravity, and unleash total chaos to save your friends from the dreaded Bacon Factory! Jhow is a brilliant, tech-obsessed piglet whose peaceful farm life is shattered when an ominous corporate truck kidnaps all his friends.

Black Lily’s Tale (1000-REKA, 29th Oct, $13.00) - Includes a Nintendo Switch™-exclusive After Story & all DLC scenarios! ―――What is Black Lily's Tale? "Black Lily's Tale", featuring delicate and beautiful art by Fukahire. A unique choice-making systems that will have you seeing visual novel decisions in a whole new light. Pure but not naive, classic but not cliché. A yuri game that will make you strive toward the best ending! You can intervene and lead these girls to happiness.

Castlebound (Ogre Pixel, 11th Nov, $9.99) - Fight hordes of evil monsters and defend your castle in this 1-4 player action platformer with Roguelike elements! Castlebound is a thrilling roguelike action game where you and your allies must defend a walking castle while battling relentless waves of monstrous foes.

Cat-Astrophy (Pdpartid@games, 5th Nov, $14.99) - Cat-Astrophy is a fast-paced, challenging space action roguelite: its Star Cursor system and evolving modules force you to adapt your build and playstyle in every run, generating chaotic combat and precise jumps. The game delivers constant tension and rewards both improvisation and technical mastery.

Don Bradman Cricket JR (Tru Blu Games, 5th Nov, $19.99) - Out of the highly successful Don Bradman simulation series comes Don Bradman JR, the hard-hitting arcade cricket game. Step onto the pitch and feel the thrill of every shot. Don Bradman Cricket JR is fast, accessible cricket that's easy to learn and rewarding to master. Smash boundaries, outplay opponents and make every run count. Pick up and play with intuitive controls. Every delivery is a contest: read the line, time the shot, find the gap. Got five minutes? Play a fast match. Got the afternoon? Play the full cricket experience.

Dungeon Of Dragon Knight Remake (Shanghai QuanYu Network Technology, 5th Nov, $14.99) - Dungeon Of Dragon Knight Remake is a first-person dungeon-crawling RPG inspired by classic role-playing adventures. Create your own party and venture deep into dangerous dungeons filled with monsters, traps, puzzles and hidden secrets. Carefully explore your surroundings, discover concealed passages and mechanisms, collect weapons, armor and useful items, and strengthen your party through battle.

EGGCONSOLE Harry Fox MSX Special MSX (D4 Enterprise, 5th Nov, $6.49) - This title is an adventure game originally released by Microcabin in 1986. While retaining the touching core story—a mother fox setting off toward the distant Reel Shrine in search of fried tofu (abura-age), rumored to be a miracle cure for her terminally ill kit—this unique MSX arranged port drastically overhauls the original gameplay systems. The game has evolved into a deeply engaging, RPG-like experience.

Eternal Palace Sakura (Shochiku, 5th Nov, $11.99) - Eternal Palace Sakura is a fast-paced, exhilarating roguelite 3D action game set in a fantastical Japanese-style dungeon that never stops changing shape. Take control of Retla, a dual-blade-wielding heroine, and face countless trials as you climb toward the top of a beautiful labyrinth where cherry blossoms drift through the air. Enjoy intuitive combo action and strategic build crafting, combining different skills and power-up items on every run.

Faraway (Annapurna Interactive, 5th Nov, $7.99) - Faraway is an endless procedurally generated, mastery-driven arcade game about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive. Connect stars to harvest their energy, extend your fleeting life, and build your score. Shape constellations freely, and take risks with advanced techniques to earn additional energy and points. Faraway’s simple rule-set and flowing controls are easy to approach but demanding to master.

Gemporium (Merge Conflict Studio, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Grow your small gem business in this short, casual simulation miner, Gemporium! Manage your time wisely between mining gemstones, refining them for more profit, and selling them to awaiting customers. After your Grandmole goes on vacation, you’re in charge of running her shop, and you quickly learn it also comes with a price of massive debt. Now, on top of building your business, you must appease the Loan Shark without going broke!

Hasbro Games Junior Collection (Outright Games, 6th Nov, $29.99) - Play Monopoly Jr., Clue Jr., and The Game of Life Jr. Customize your avatar, unlock rewards, and enjoy local multiplayer fun for up to 4 players. Get ready for a big, colorful game night full of laughs, surprises, and “just one more turn!” moments! This collection brings 3 classic junior board games to life in one exciting video game made for kids and families.

Hillthorn (Raw Fury, 10th Nov, $14.99) - Only the foolish and the desperate attempt to wander the mazelike trails of Hillthorn. Even those who know their way may still stumble upon dangerous wildlife or a local villager’s piercing gaze. But a child has gone missing, time is in short supply, and you’re the one being tasked with unraveling the mountain’s secrets. Welcome to Hillthorn, a dark investigation game unlike any other, where the mystery unfolds without a single word spoken.

HorrorVale: Deadluxe Edition (Electric Airship, 31st Oct, $17.99) - Your next-door neighbors are zombies, reanimated monsters deliver the mail and ghosts hide out in your bathroom. Don't worry about anybody you kill along the way–-everyone is already dead! Muahahha! Bash monsters, recruit 30+ friends, and solve brain-buster puzzles! Welcome to the Underworld. . .

Hundred Fires: OPEN VECTOR -Episode 1- (David Amado Fernández, 29th Oct, $6.99) - HUNDRED FIRES: OPEN VECTOR — Episode 1 is a third-person action and stealth adventure set in an alternate Cold War. You play as Merche, a guerrilla and expert thief sent on a mission that quickly turns into something much bigger. Armed with a katana, a pistol and automatic weapons, you'll have to infiltrate secret facilities, deal with enemy soldiers and uncover the secrets behind the mysterious Ancient Weapons. The katana is at the heart of the game. Use it in combat, but also use it to cut through parts of the environment.

Kingdom of Night (DANGEN Entertainment, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Kingdom of Night is an 80s-inspired isometric action RPG where coming-of-age drama meets cosmic horror. When a satanic cult unleashes the ancient evil Baphomet on the small town of Miami, Arizona, high school student John must fight through a night of demonic chaos to rescue his friends before the town is lost forever. Choose from five distinct classes—Barbarian, Knight, Rogue, Necromancer, or Sorcerer—and customize your build with expansive skill trees, powerful loot, and unique equipment.

K-Pop Rising – Dream to Shine (Microids, 5th Nov, $34.99) - Make your dream come true and become a K-Pop Star in this exciting life sim and rhythm game! Together with your best friend Nova, you've always dreamed of making your mark in the world of K-Pop… Now it's time to shine! Throw yourself into the race for fame and let your talent sparkle, from the practice rooms to the stage! Create a group that reflects who you are and, together, set out to conquer the world's biggest stages. Take inspiration from your idols and grow your fan community on social media! Music is your world, and passion is your driving force: you are the future of K-Pop!

LightQb (Restless Corp, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Twenty-three handcrafted levels. One directional dash. And a narrator who will not let a single mistake go unmentioned. LightQb is a fast, unforgiving first-person platformer built entirely around movement. Chain dashes, air control and raw momentum to fly through neon structures, then do it all again a second faster.

Lilac ~side Witch~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Lilac ~side Wizard~ (Frontwing, 5th Nov, $24.99) - A fantasy visual novel set in a magic school where humans and mages mingle. Follow Emil, a young human who despises mages, and Henri, a self-proclaimed "bonehead" of a mage, as they learn how to connect in spite of various anxieties and differing backgrounds. Features numerous beautiful characters designed by industry veteran Oyari Ashito! Lilac Academy.

Make it! Karaage (SAT-BOX, 5th Nov, $6.99) - Let's make karaage on Nintendo Switch! Marinate the meat in sauce, coat it in batter, and fry it until crispy! Pack up the finished karaage and add toppings to match each order! Share Joy-Con, and up to 4 players can play together! Reach for the ultimate high score! Make karaage to order! Keep cooking until time runs out!

Next of Kin: Epiphany (Spelkvall, 5th Nov, $9.99) - Step into the world of "Next of Kin: Epiphany," where you become private detective Dennis Monroe, a relentless investigator driven to catch the infamous "Epiphany Killer," a shadowy figure who has haunted the city for over twenty years. Every clue draws you closer to the truth, but danger lurks behind every revelation. In the thrilling conclusion to the "Next of Kin" trilogy, you'll explore atmospheric locations, interrogate suspects with the powerful new "Expose" system, and unravel the chilling truth behind the notorious "Epiphany Killer".

Nyghtmare: The Ninth King (Caracal Games, 31st Oct, $4.99) - Centuries after vanishing without a trace, the Kingdom of Mortemire suddenly reappears. Alongside it awakens Aryn, a young woman strangely unaffected by the mysterious call surrounding the kingdom. Armed with only an iron whip, she ventures into its decaying streets in search of answers, facing the creatures and dangers that have taken hold of the land. Nyghtmare: The Ninth King is a dark-fantasy retro "Vania" experience.

Prinny Party: Going Overboard! (NIS America, 11th Nov, $29.99) - Get your friends together for Prinny Party: Going Overboard! In this party game, you’ll traverse the board as you take down demons, earn experience, and buy new equipment—all to make sure you’re strong enough to beat Laharl, the Supreme Overboard!

Shelterra the Skyworld (KEMCO, 5th Nov, $17.99) - Soar into an epic fantasy RPG adventure across Shelterra, a vast floating continent untouched by the mysterious corruption known as Odium. Claude dreams of becoming a professional adventurer, but a simple escort mission soon reveals a threat that could send his entire homeland crashing to the surface.

Shrek 2 Remastered (Aspyr, 10th Nov, $26.99) - Journey through the fairytale kingdom of Far Far Away from Shrek’s swamp to Fiona’s castle and everywhere in between, in a classic action-adventure experience inspired by the DreamWorks Animation movie. Play solo or with up to three friends in co-op, take control of your favorite Shrek heroes as you smash, throw and kick your way against iconic characters from the franchise.

The Slormancer (Plug In Digital, 5th Nov, $24.99) - The Slormancer is an epic 2D Action-RPG Dungeon Crawling game following a band of outcasts on their fight against hordes of enemies led by The Slormancer! Play as a Mighty Knight, a Fierce Huntress or a Mischievous Mage, master hundreds of abilities and ancestral powers, gear up, fight for the reputation of your kind and prove your value to the realm. Experience fast-paced gameplay, loads of shiny loot, tons of collectibles, countless hours of content, and carefully crafted pixel art. You were born with absolutely no skill whatsoever, and yet you find a way to be the last hope of the realm as the enigmatic Slormancer and his incompetent underling try to conquer the world once again. How great. But like your grandfather once told you: "You might not have the talent but you have the will."

The Transference (JanduSoft, 29th Oct, $9.99) - YOUR OWN HOME HAS BECOME AN ESCAPE ROOM. AND YOU'RE NOT ALONE. The Transference is a first-person mystery thriller escape room that combines puzzles, a story of family secrets, and moments of tension where you'll have to hide to survive. WHO LOCKED YOU IN? AND WHY? You wake up in your home and discover that the doors and windows have been boarded up from the inside. Someone has placed strange riddles throughout the rooms and turned your home into a prison. Explore, search for clues, and find a way out while trying to answer one question: who is behind all this? PUT YOUR WITS TO THE TEST

The Trolley Solution (Take IT Studio!, 29th Oct, $9.99) - Philosophers already waste their time and lives thinking about thinking. Why not have fun while doing it? The Trolley Solution is a compilation of minigames based on the famous trolley problem, originally proposed in 1967 by British philosopher Philippa Foot. Put your thinking power to the test in humorous iterations of the problem. Unlock a variety of minigames where you can put your gaming skills to the test. Challenge yourself and learn important and useful philosophical knowledge while expanding your mind! Disclaimer: You might not actually learn anything useful or important, nor expand your mind, by playing this game.

Titanium Court (Fellow Traveller, 29th Oct, $11.24) - Well what do we have here? Streetwise tough looking for answers, huh. Well, answers we got, assuming you've got the second half of our agreement? Excellent. Love the satisfying click of an opening briefcase. Come on in, pal. Here's all the "dirt" we uncovered on this "Titanium Court": So, lotta people have heard of this game, but not a lot are coming clean about what it actually is. Most of the witnesses we "interviewed" just said it was "a fanciful rabbit-hole of unending delights" or some crap like that. Real coy operation they got going on over there, I'll tell ya what. Don't worry, we did manage to shake a few facts out of them. Here you go! Title: Titanium Court Developer: AP Thomson Publisher: Fellow Traveller Number of players: 1 Play time: 6-30 hours. Now as for the genre we were having a lot of trouble pinning that down from testimony alone, so we "acquired" a copy to see what was up. (Hey what's a private investigation without a little bit of larceny, right?

UNDERGROUNDED (room6, 29th Oct, $19.99) - Scott, a young man from Manhattan, finally pops the question to his girlfriend. . . who promptly says "no. " He's so dejected that he accidentally drops the ring he used to propose into a storm drain. The ring keeps falling deeper and deeper underground. It falls into the sewers, then further down into. . . a movie theater? Wait, is that a jet plane? Why are we in the Old West now? What are cowboys doing underground? ? ?

Unpetrified: Echoes of Nature (Mindscape, 10th Nov, $29.99) - Unpetrified: Echoes of Nature is a peaceful and reflective experience, filled with meaningful collectibles, unique emotion-driven interactions, and environmental puzzles. The orchestral soundtrack emphasizes an intimate storyline of unlikely friendship, loss, and love.

VALKYRIE TUNE：Synthesis of Souls (Good Smile Company, 5th Nov, $24.99) - Story An intertwining, resonant serenade of love, sorrow, and fateful encounters calls forth a reboot for the future. Step into the shoes of Rei, who wakes up in the Domed City of Initium surrounded by women calling him the Messiah. Determined to regain the memories he lost during years of cryosleep, he begins living with the six beautiful members of the TUNED (Tactical Unit for Neutralization and Enhanced Defense)-young women who wield so-called harmonic weapons.

Warhammer Survivors (Auroch Digital, 10th Nov, $7.19) - Warhammer Survivors is a fast-paced roguelite survivors' game, pitting a host of iconic Warhammer characters against endless hordes of enemies from multiple Warhammer factions. Developed by Auroch Digital (Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun) in partnership with Warhammer and poncle (Vampire Survivors), discover the universes of Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer: Age of Sigmar in all its pixel glory in this new surviv-a-ton.

#4265. 35 million of you have already pre-registered for Arknights: Endfield

Ahead of its official release next week, Arknights: Endfield has already surpassed 35 million pre-registrations from players around the world.

Arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer announced today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer said at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also shows off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

You can expect more Arknights: Endfield coverage from us at release and beyond. In fact, based on what we played so far, we’re pretty confident in this early Arknights Endfield characters list.

#4264. Sony Has Secured Enough Memory to Meet Console Demand Through March 2028

Amid ever-increasing hardware prices, driven by an AI-led drain on memory components, Sony has reassured investors that it’s secured enough inventory to meet its hardware projections through March 2028.

In its new financial report, the manufacturer acknowledged the following:

“Regarding memory procurement for next fiscal year, based on discussions held so far with various suppliers, we have aligned on the quantity of memory needed for our projected hardware unit sales.”

Obviously we don’t know what its projections for the next fiscal year are just yet, and whether it’ll need to adjust the price of the PS5 again in the new year. But it will at least have inventory to ship, which is important.

It’s going to be really interesting to see whether its next fiscal year will include the PS6 or not.

Sony says it’s making “solid progress” on the system, but it’s still unclear whether it’ll ship in 2027 or later.

Xbox, for the record, has said it plans to ship a new handheld in 2027 and its next console in 2028. Its price could run as high as $1,800 – although it’s expected the PS6 will be cheaper to manufacture overall. (Although potentially still $1,000+.)

This is a tricky period for manufacturers of all consumer electronics, but PS5’s enormous captive install base has shielded it slightly from the repercussions so far.

In its latest fiscal report, it revealed an 83% increase to its operating income, meaning the profitability of PlayStation is in an extremely steady and healthy position right now.

#4263. AMD FSR Upscaling 4.1 Has Officially Arrived For Xbox Series X|S

"We can't wait to see what developers create with it."

A couple of weeks ago, the folks at AMD made headlines when they announced that AMD FSR 4.1 would be coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S in the near future, and the rollout has officially begun today!

As a result of this, developers will have access to a new method of improving visual fidelity (and in some cases boosting performance) in their games across both consoles, which should prove particularly useful when it comes to the lower-powered Xbox Series S.

"Working closely with AMD, the XBOX team has optimized AMD FSR™ Upscaling 4 for XBOX Series X|S, making ML-based upscaling practical on the consoles' RDNA 2-based GPUs. These optimizations enable developers to benefit from improved image quality while balancing GPU performance, helping them deliver better visual experiences on existing XBOX hardware."

"The new Microsoft GDK sample demonstrates how to integrate FSR4 across XBOX Series X|S and Windows using AMD’s FSR SDK. It includes both Full and Lite INT8 models, allowing developers to explore different rendering resolutions and evaluate the tradeoffs between image quality and performance."

Of course, it's still early days right now and we don't have any real-world examples of AMD FSR 4.1 working on XBOX Series X|S just yet, but we assume developers of all kinds will start integrating it into their games going forward.

Not only should this lead to improved experiences in demanding XBOX Series X|S titles, but it should also mean the two consoles remain capable for many years to come, even after Project Helix arrives in the next generation.

News AMD FSR 4.1 Announced For Xbox Series X|S And ROG Xbox Handhelds

"And there's even more ahead with Project Helix..."

News Xbox Working 'Very Closely' With AMD To Improve Ray Tracing & Other FSR Features In Games

As part of the new AMD Redstone technology

Excited to see what developers can do with AMD FSR 4.1 on Xbox consoles? Tell us down below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

@Banjo- Logically, Rockstar will apply it to GTA VI, because it's a very simple feature to implement.

As for your comparison with QSSR, it is currently only supported by two games on PS5: Wolverine and Ghost of Yōtei. At this stage, it is mostly a marketing feature with very little real impact for players. In reality, AMD's QSSR is derived from FSR, but in a much more limited form because, as you mentioned, the base PS5 lacks some native hardware features that are available on the Xbox Series consoles.

Furthermore, it is more complex for third-party developers, as it requires genuine porting work. As a result, this technology will likely remain limited to a small number of PlayStation-exclusive titles.

FSR, on the other hand, is a technology that has been deployed much more broadly by game developers, as it is already widely used on PC.

The case of PlayStation's PSSR, which is only available on the PS5 Pro, is different. The PS5 Pro already includes more native hardware capabilities than the base PS5 and is significantly more powerful. Even then, PSSR is also derived from FSR 4, although it still does not match FSR 4 at equivalent hardware performance levels. PSSR has seen greater adoption among developers, but the numbers remain relatively modest in practice. We're talking about roughly 200 games that support PSSR, which is still a small figure compared to the total number of games released each year.

What is certain is that PlayStation's marketing around GTA VI is misleading, or at the very least requires significant nuance. If we're talking about the base PS5, then the claim is false: GTA VI would run better on Xbox Series consoles with FSR 4.1.2. On PS5 Pro, however, GTA VI would likely perform better, which is hardly surprising given that it is a more powerful mid-generation refresh released later and sold at a significantly higher price. However, its price-to-performance ratio remains relatively poor.

Given the relatively small install base of the PS5 Pro compared to the standard PS5, the Xbox Series remains the most obvious value-for-money choice for the majority of players interested in GTA VI.

The claim that GTA VI or other games runs better on PS5 is simply false, on the contrary.

#4262. 'Aggressive Investment in Entertainment Is Paying Off': Sony Lifts Profit Outlook After Strong Quarter

Sony’s transition away from electronics and into entertainment is paying serious dividends, after a killer quarter has prompted it to lift its operating income outlook for the fiscal year through March 2027.

The Japanese giant now expects to pull ¥1.87 trillion (~$11.8 billion) in profit, up 15% on its previous prediction.

In its Q2 report, the period spanning July 206 through September 2026, it posted operating income of ¥622.3 billion (~$3.9 billion) alone, beating pretty much all analyst predictions.

At the time of writing, its stock price is up 7% on the back of these results.

Hideki Yasuda of Toyo Research and Advice Co told Bloomberg:

"Today’s results clearly show the payoff from Sony’s aggressive investment in content over the past several years, across movies, games and music. When Sony was more hardware-driven, its earnings were much more volatile."

As mentioned, Sony can thank its investment into entertainment for the positive results, at a time when the consumer electronics market is strained due to component prices.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day, the acclaimed Tom Holland movie, was a huge win for Sony Pictures, meanwhile PlayStation continued its momentum with another excellent quarter for PS5.

Sony Music also saw increases on the back of its co-ownership of Michael Jackson’s music catalogue, which saw an enormous increase in streams due to the release of the Michael biopic earlier in the year.

Despite all these wins in entertainment, the firm’s image sensing business also saw improvements to profitability, despite a global decline in smartphone sales.

All things said, the Japanese company finds itself in an incredibly healthy position, and its big business bets all appear to be paying off at the moment.

#4260. "You Don't Want To Interrupt The Player's Experience" - Here's Why Zelda's Switch 2 Remake Cut Some Mario References

Nintendo is known in recent times for dropping Star Fox (and even Pikmin) into the Super Mario universe, but with the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Switch 2, it decided to take a little more care.

In the castle courtyard, where Link meets with Zelda, you might have noticed how the character portraits for Mario and friends are not in the Switch 2 version of the game. If you are wondering about the thought process behind this, Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma has explained how the team didn't want to break the immersion.

Here's what he had to say during the same chat with Game Informer:

Eiji Aonuma: "Certainly, at the time, when we put those [portraits] there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal. Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing. But looking at it now, like if a player is coming through that area, and given the overall way that we're, you know, creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, "Why is Yoshi there?” We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

If you recall, the 3DS game also had Skyward Sword art hidden in certain locations, and this is also gone from the Switch 2 remake. According to Aonuma, the same reasoning applies here - the team didn't want to "interrupt the player's experience by seeing something that's unrelated to what they're currently doing in the game".

Although these easter eggs are gone, certain references to the Mario series remain intact as they are part of the character designs:

"You will remember that there is one design element on Talon with Bowser on it, and that's part of the original design of the character. So we didn't change that. That stays as is."

News "I'll Leave It To Your Imagination" - Aonuma's Keeping Quiet On Bombchu Girl's Relationship Status

News "I'm On A Mission" - Miyamoto Wants To Include Pikmin In Any Kind Of Nintendo Product He Can

News Super Mario Galaxy Movie Directly Led To New Star Fox And Yoshi Games, Miyamoto Confirms

What are your thoughts about this decision? Did you notice the change yourself? Let us know in the comments.

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters.

I wish they had kept the Mario reference in the courtyard window but made it only viewable if you stood in just the right place.

But at the same time, they changed a lot of things that were familiar to me about the original to reach kids whose parents might not even have been alive when the original came out.

There’s no reason they need to treat an all-time classic as a museum piece, because the original game will always be a masterpiece. Better to iterate upon it with fresh ideas and convenient tweaks than to declare any changes off-limits because of Nostalgia™.

The only major thing I would have done differently is to preserve the more poetic and succinct quality of the original English translation. I understand why they changed it for new audiences, but I still miss the original’s grand tone, and that’s one reason the 64 and 3DS versions will always have a place for me.

In general immersion is not something I have ever remotely cared about and I'd a lot rather just keep the random goofy references, but it's also not exactly a dealbreaker.
